blocks.content: The Supreme Court famously criticized the agency during the Coal Block Allocation case, calling it a 'caged parrot speaking in its master's voice'.

rows: Default consent given by states to seamlessly investigate central employees/crimes in their jurisdiction
Prior permission required on a case-by-case basis before registering a fresh investigation
CBI loses authority to register new cases in the state without explicit state approval
Required whenever General Consent is withdrawn; ongoing cases prior to withdrawal remain unaffected

items: CBI is NOT a statutory body (it was created by an executive resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs).
Section 6 of the DSPE Act renders state government consent mandatory for CBI investigations within state jurisdiction.
The selection committee for the CBI Director was modified by the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: CBI is not a statutory body; it derives its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
The CBI Director is provided a security of tenure of two years under the CVC Act, 2003, extendable up to five years through annual extensions.

The Director is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a three-member committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition (or single largest opposition party), and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by them.
State consent under Section 6 of the DSPE Act is mandatory for the CBI to exercise powers and jurisdiction in any state area.
